A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ETA framework with matching authors, methods, and principal experiments. The text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original safety, helpfulness, efficiency, and ablation experiments, including Tables 1–10 and appendix case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds embedding-mapping results, newer-backbone evaluations, MMMU-Pro results, and an additional case study.

M1.justification: The CLIP and reward-model evaluators, requirement that both flag unsafe behavior, interference prefix, and sentence-level best-of-N alignment remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 and scoring equations are retained. The added explanation that sentence candidates condition on preceding sentences clarifies the existing procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds VLSafe to the embedding-mapping analysis and MMMU-Pro to evaluate multidisciplinary understanding and reasoning. Figure 6 also introduces a benign crime-prevention request involving potentially unsafe imagery. These are bounded extensions of the existing safety and usefulness coverage; previous datasets and tasks remain.

E2.justification: v2 Table 7 adds vanilla LLaVA-NeXT-8B, LLaVA-OneVision-7B-Chat, and Llama3.2-11B-Vision-Instruct as controls against their ETA-equipped counterparts. Existing ECSO and VLGuard Posthoc-LoRA/Mixed-LoRA comparisons are retained. No additional competing defense algorithm is evaluated; the added Llama Guard citation is not an experimental comparator.

E3.justification: Added experiments introduce a random 100-example VLSafe sample, additional backbone configurations, and MMMU-Pro's Standard (4 Options) + Direct and Vision + Direct settings. Existing evaluation metrics, attack procedures, thresholds of 0.16/0.06, and five sentence candidates remain unchanged. These are additional settings, not documented reruns under revised original protocols.

E4.justification: v2 substantially broadens the empirical test of the central embedding hypothesis: the cosine-mapping check illustrated for LLaVA-1.5-7B on SPA-VL in v1 Figure 2 is extended across four backbones and two datasets in v2 Table 6. Appendix B.8/Figure 6 also adds an excessive-conservatism case study. Existing component ablations and threshold analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the benchmark results. The existing reward-distribution and KL-divergence displays remain unchanged. Randomly sampling VLSafe examples changes the evaluation design, not uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: All ten original tables retain their numerical results, but v2 adds substantial results in Tables 6, 7, and 11. For example, Table 7 reports FigStep-suffix USR of 44.00 versus 3.20 for vanilla Llama3.2 and its ETA counterpart; Table 11 reports identical MMMU-Pro scores with and without ETA across six backbones. These are newly reported comparisons, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6, the safety-score definitions, and the appendix metric formulas are unchanged. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs. The expanded embedding-mapping evidence is empirical rather than a new mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same training-free ETA contribution, embedding-based explanation of safety failures, and safety/usefulness claims. The headline 87.5% unsafe-rate reduction and 96.6% helpfulness win-tie rate are unchanged; additional experiments support the existing claims.

C2.justification: Section 5.3 replaces the claim of improved helpfulness without compromising harmlessness with an explicit tradeoff: adding utility guidance increases Helpful Score by 0.12 and USR by 0.38 percentage points, using unchanged Table 5 results. New Appendix B.8 explains how the dual-evaluator criterion can avoid excessive conservatism, illustrated by one benign-request example.

D1.justification: v2 adds a reproducibility statement reporting downloadable implementation code in supplementary materials and explicitly documents conditioning sentence candidates on previous sentences. Both versions already provide the public code link, evaluator prompts, hardware, thresholds, and candidate count. The PDFs establish added documentation, not verified changes in external resource availability.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for LLaVA-NeXT, LLaVA-OneVision, MMMU/MMMU-Pro, Llama Guard, and Tu et al.'s VLM safety benchmark. These support the additional evaluations and contextual discussion. The central positioning against fine-tuning, ECSO, and AdaShield remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most main-text prose and the overall narrative are retained. v2 makes local explanatory edits, adds a reproducibility statement and appendix subsections, and swaps the order of baseline details and GPT-4 evaluation details in Appendix A. This is limited reorganization rather than extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 6, 7, and 11 and the case-study Figure 6, while relocating and renumbering existing appendix displays. Conference headers and local page layouts change, but the principal diagrams, existing plots, and original table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: Relative to v1's already extensive evaluation, v2 provides useful additional support for the embedding hypothesis, applicability to newer VLMs, and preservation of harder reasoning performance. It also describes Table 5's safety–helpfulness tradeoff more accurately. The new excessive-conservatism claim exceeds the support of its single example, but the broader empirical evidence and clearer interpretation provide a limited net improvement.
